events.notes: Perfect D1 in both formats. Tougher D2, obviously, reaching 3-3, giving him two win-and-ins for T8. He lost to Seth Manfield, and then Christoffer Larsen in R16.
The deepest of holes at 0-4, knuckled down to make D2, and then 6-2 D2, long after T8 hopes were gone.
After a 4-3-1 D1, four wins in a row brought him into the mix, before Daniel Goetschel beat him in R13 to end his chances.
A day of two halves. Perfect in Draft, 3-0. Nothing in Standard, 0-4, no D2.
Only one win in each format, so no D2.
Three draws were an important part of his story, since he only lost four times all tournament, but the draws were more than enough to keep him away from T8, despite 4-1 down the stretch in Modern.
4-4 overnight, and soon out of contention. Won his last three to have a winning record.
3-3, but lost both his last two rounds, so no D2.
An excellent 5-0 start saw him contend deep into D2, with Tomasz Sodomirski ending his chances in R14.
0-3 Draft, won the first round of Standard, but that was all.
4-1 was only the beginning, as he then won eight straight to reach the T8 with a staggering three rounds to spare. QFs were a big letdown, being swept by Derrick Davis.
A rollercoaster. 6-0, then 6-4 to be on the edge, up to 8-4, then elimination from contention.
Out of the running by R10, but still had five wins in a row D2.
4-2-1 overnight, but 0-3 in D2 Draft to take him out of the running.
Strong start at 4-1, but couldn't build from there.
Won opening Draft, and had two more three win streaks. Two D1 draws were costly, however.
From 3-1, 4-4 overnight was a disappointment. Soon out of contention.
In trouble at 1-2, didn't lose for a day, reaching 8-2 heading back to Standard. Losses to Seth Manfield and Kai Budde left him on the edge, and a final round loss to Lucas Duchow meant no T8.
Won his opening Draft, advanced to 6-2, and still in the mix before Socrates Rozakeas ended his run in R14.
1-3 meant afterburners required. Seven wins followed, but, once back in Pioneer, Sean Goddard and Javier Dominguez gave him too much to do.
Streaks of four and three wins kept him in the mix, until two Standard draws on D2 cost him too many points.
Comfortably made D2, but 1-2 in Draft ended his chances.
Couldn't recover from the worst possible 0-3 Draft start, with just a single win.
Very much alive at 7-3, but that was all the winning done.
Things to build on, with a pair of 2-1s in Draft. 4-6 in Pioneer.
From 4-3, won six of his next seven to keep him live for T8 with two rounds to go, before Derrick Davis took him out in R15.

Three sets of three straight wins kept him in contention throughout, but a R12 defeat to Javier Dominguez meant he needed four straight to finish, and he fell one short, with Yiwen Chen advancing to the T8.
5-3 overnight, but began D2 with a loss. Four straight wins kept him alive back in Modern, before Marco Cammilluzzi finished his contention in R14.
After three straight D2s, this was a D1 horror show, with just one win in each format.
At 5-1 things were looking great. Five rounds later, he was done at 5-6, including an 0-3 Draft.
5-3 overnight, but another D2 0-3 Draft eliminated him from contention.

Still only 1-1-1 in Draft on D2, but this time it didn't matter. 6-2 on D1, and then a 4-1 record in Modern took him into the T8. He edged out Noah Ma in the QFs before losing the deciding game in the Semis against Simon Nielsen.
Stood at 3-3, before mini-nemesis Derrick Davis eliminated him from D2.
Won three in a row to reach 3-1, but no wins after that.
Twice won three in a row, but couldn't overcome 2-4 in Draft.
Started out 1-1, before four straight losses eliminated him from Day 2. Won four games, but a tough day.
Tough road from 1-1, including losses to Autumn Burchett and Eli Loveman. Out after R6.
From 3-3 to 3-5, so no D2.
Excellent 5-1 in Draft, but only 5-5 in Standard.
Excellent 6-1-1 D1, but couldn't maintain the pace D2.
From 3-2 to 3-5, losing all three chances to advance by 2-1. Tough.
From 1-1, went on a stupendous eleven round win streak, meaning T8 qualification with a ridiculous three rounds to spare. Lost QFs to Daniel Goetschel in a full five game set.
1-3, recovered to make D2, then 5-3, but never in serious contention.
Draft 3-0 into excellent 7-1 D1. Lost to Nathan Steuer and Javier Dominguez in successive rounds, but then won four straight in Standard to reach the T8. Narrowly lost to Autumn Burchett in the QFs.
One of the greatest starts ever, reaching 12-0, and making a second successive T8. Beat Stefano Vinci in the QFs, before Christian Calcano edged him out in G5 of the Semis.

A THIRD T8 in a row, this time from a precarious 0-2. Ten wins in a row followed, frankly absurd numbers. Beat Lorenzo Terlizzi in the QFs, but was swept by Kazune Kosaka in the Semis. Nonetheless, and incredible season.

A stupendous four in a row, despite, for him, an only average 4-2 Draft record. With Boros Heroic, he went 8-2, then took it past Adam Edelson and Christoffer Larsen, before losing the Final to Seth Manfield, setting up an epic Player of the Year race in the process.

A brilliant D2 that began 6-0 was wasted by a haphazard D1 that ended at the minimum 4-4. It still took Javier Dominguez in the penultimate round to prevent a fifth T8 in a row. Literally extraordinary.

Another Draft pod aced to open, 6-2 overnight, but needed three straight wins to reach T8. Got them, of course. This time he went the distance, edging past Javier Dominguez and Daniel Goetschel before taking down Sam Pardee in the Finals to complete one of the greatest sequences of anyone ever.
Somehow 6-0 in Draft wasn't enough momentum, with a 2-2 on D1 in Standard becoming a nightmare 0-4 on D2.
Trophy in Draft 1, and added a 2-1 in Draft on D2. Losing record in Standard, however.
5-3 overnight into 4-4 D2. Never managed three wins in a row.

A perfect 8-0 D1; a 1-3 wobble to start D2; then three straight wins to secure T8. From there, beat the mighty Gabriel Nassif 3-1, and Takumi Matsuura 3-0 in the Semis, before Reid Duke was too much to handle in the Finals.
Won R1, but not much else.
From 1-3, five straight wins put him back into the mix, and he lasted until R13 before fading.
4-3 overnight, before three wins kept him alive to the penultimate round, where Mitchell Tamblyn ended things.
3-0 opening Draft, a solid 5-3 D1 overall, but lost three of his last four on D2 to fade.
Needed two wins to advance, got them, and then put together a solid 5-3 on D2 without ever threatening the T8.
After 4-1 became a disappointing 4-4, a Draft pod win to start D2 put him in contention. Two wins from five in Pioneer D2 didn't get it done.
After a R9 draw left him on the verge of elimination he rattled off seven straight wins, but, though barely, it was not enough - the draw cost him dear.
For the third event running, he scraped into D2. This time there was no solid recovery.

4-3 on D1 turned into 6-1 on D2, taking him into the T8, where he faced Kazune Kosaka for a second time. And, for a second time, Kosaka's Esper Midrange deck defeated him, leaving Edel out in the QFs.
3-1 was a strong start. Four defeats turned it around in a hurry.
Nicely in contention heading back to Standard on D2, but losses to Eli Kassis and Marco Del Pivo ended his run.
Plenty of work to do at 4-4, he opened D2 by winning his Draft pod, but then lost three straight in Modern to end things.
A solid 5-2 D1, but three defeats in a row on D2 were too much, despite winning his last three of the day.
1-2 in Draft, no wins in Pioneer, out after R6.
6-4 in Modern, 3-3 in Draft not enough.
Lone win was in Draft.
A pair of solid 2-1s in Draft, but just even at 5-5 in Pioneer, which was disappointing having started out 4-0 in the constructed format.
0-4 became 3-4, but lost the final round.
2-0 to 2-4 to making D2, then a solid 5-3, but never in the mix.
Just a single D1 win, so no D2.
Won four of his last five, but was already out of contention.
A glimpse of the Stark of Ago, opening 6-2 D1, and still in the mix down the stretch, before Arne Huschenbeth beat him twice on D2 to take him out of contention.
5-3 on D1, but D2 Draft pod win was the springboard for T8, winning 7 from 8 on D2. Swept Shota Yasooka in the QFs before a 3-1 defeat to eventual champion Reid Duke in the Semis.
Four wins on the bounce to reach 4-1 was the highlight, with 1-2 in Ltd on D2 eliminating him from contention before the return to Standard.
Very swingy event, with both four and five win streaks, separated by four defining losses to end D1 and start D2.
Beaten twice by Matt Foreman, he was never above .500, and didn't make D2.
Aced his opening Draft, but only 1-4 on D1 Pioneer. Out of contention after R9, finished even at 8-8.
From 0-2 to 5-3 was a solid D1, but another 1-2 Draft on D2 eliminated him from contention.
Solid four wins on the bounce left him at 7-2, but then eliminated by a combination of Shuhei Nakamura, Nathan Steuer, and Greg Orange.
4-3 became 6-3, live for Top 8. Alex Friedrichsen ended his contention in R12, leaving Davis to win his last two, ending a strong 9-5.
Needed three straight to advance from 1-4, got the first two, but not the last.
4-3 overnight, reversed on D2.
Terrific 6-1-1 D1, hung around until R14, eliminated from contention by Jim Davis.
4-1-1 start, but couldn't quite accelerate, just 4-4 D2.
Five straight wins the backbone of another solid effort. D2 once again challenging, going 3-4-1
Disaster. Came with nothing, left with nothing.
Turned 0-3 around to make D2, and scraped above halfway with a 4-3-1 record there. Never in contention.
Opened 2-2, but couldn’t buy a win from there.
Twice had four straight wins, but lost three in a row down the stretch to take him out of contention.
Needed a R8 win to make D2, improved with 5-2-1 on D2, but never in contention.
4-4 overnight, so even a 6-2 D2 couldn't get him into the mix.
Matching 4-4 records both days, and only 4-6 with the deck of the tournament in Pioneer.

Paced the field at 6-0, so disappointing to end D1 6-2. Back on track with Draft pod win D2, then fought an absurd slate of opponents in Standard, beating Javier Dominguez in R16 to reach the T8. He beat Lucas Duchow in the QFs, before Yoshihko Ikawa beat him for the second time in the competition, this time in the SFs.
3-0 Draft to start, but fell away badly on D2, with three losses and a draw a four round stretch he couldn't recover from.
One win in each format nowhere near enough for D2.
Four straight wins on D1 was still only enough for 4-4, and then four straight defeats was more than enough to see him out of contention.
Eli won all three Draft rounds on D1, but the pod went to Eli Loveman!
Never quite had the momentum, and three wins R12-14 were too late to matter.
Won his D1 Draft, then 5-2 overnight, before another pod win to start D2. At 8-2 in tremendous shape to T8, before two losses and a draw derailed him.
6-2, then 5-3, but winning his last four matches was already irrelevant thanks to three straight losses early on D2.
Well in contention off the back of 5-1 in Draft, eliminated from contention by Nicole Tipple in R15.
Superb seven round win streak, plus three D2 Modern wins took him into T8 with two rounds to spare. Beat Seth Manfield in the QFs, before Sam Pardee took the deciding game in the Semis.
Solid 4-2 in Draft, once again in contention down the stretch at 5-1 in Standard. Losses to Javier Dominguez and Yoshihiko Ikawa in the last two rounds kept him out of the T8.
Most of his wins came in pairs, but never better off than 2-0.
From 3-1, it took until R8 to secure D2, and then only won once.
Safely into D2, but out of contention early. Impressively won his last four.
Kept winning multiple rounds without ever putting together a sizeable run. 4-1 in Standard on D2 the highlight, but already out of contention by then.
2-3 to 5-3 D1, but out of contention before the return to Modern.
Alternated wins and losses throughout D1, could only add 3-4 on D2.
5-2-1 D1 but couldn't quite kick on, despite another solid 5-3 on D2.
On the ropes at 1-4 but made D2. Couldn't quite claim his D2 Draft pod, functionally eliminating him, but still won 4 of 5 back in Standard.
Again had to win R8 to reach D2, and again took the opportunity, winning his Draft pod, going 7-1 D2, but still ending one win short of T8.
Perfect 3-0 Draft, but fell from 4-0 to 4-3 overnight. Lost an Esper Midrange mirror in R11 to end his chances.
In contention down the stretch, repairing an 0-2 start. Streaks of four and three wins took him to R14, where Logan Nettles ended his chances.
2-2 no disgrace, given the losses were to Javier Dominguez and Nathan Steuer. 5-2-1 overnight, before 1-2 Draft D2 took him out of the running.
3-1-1 before three straight defeats to miss out on D2.
A R6 draw in the Domain Ramp mirror against Mitchell Tamblyn ultimately cost him his D2 place.
Had a tough schedule (Christoffer Larsen, Javibier Dominguez, Logan Nettles) and didn't reach D2.
Solid 4-2 in Draft, 2-1 both times, but underwhelming in Standard.
A poor start to the season, only winning a single match before being dumped out after R6.
In big trouble at 2-4, he went into overdrive, winning eight straight. Brendon Johnson ended his T8 hopes in R15.
2-1 in Draft, then 6-1 before being pegged back to 6-4, with R13 ending his T8 interest.
A horrible Draft 0-3 to start, but still made D2. Draft, this time 1-2, was more than enough to eliminate him.
Perfect 3-0 in Draft to start, and still alive at 9-4 before Eli Kassis took him out in R14.
Despite being undefeated on D1 in Modern, that featured two damaging draws. Despite seven straight wins, it was once again Eli Kassis acting as nemesis, defeating him once on each day.
Another Draft pod win to start, and a solid 5-2 overnight. Couldn't repeat on D2, going 3-4 to finish a respectable 8-6.
Disappointing 2-4 in Draft, much better 7-3 in Standard.
Solid 2-1 into excellent 8-2, then 11-2. Three brutal losses, against Sam Pardee, Jean-Emmanuel Depraz, and Simon Nielsen (all win-and-ins), meant no T8.
3-0 Draft start, 6-1-1 D1, a small Draft wobble D2, before four straight Standard wins to reach T8. Lost the deciding game to Takumi Matsuura in the QFs.
Spectacular again. 0-1 to 8-1, then through to T8 with a round to spare. Lost again in a QF game five, this time against Sam Pardee.
In a 1-3 hole, made D2. Kept fighting at 6-4, but soon out of the running down the stretch.
Strong 7-3 in Standard, but only parity at 3-3 in Draft.
Trophy to open D1, and 2-1 in Draft D2. Only 4-6 in Modern, however.
0-3 and Draft, and only a single win in Pioneer before being eliminated.

One of the greatest single tournaments of all time. 3-0 Draft. 5-0 Standard. A single loss to Javier Dominguez D2 Draft. Three more Standard wins, making T8 with three rounds to spare. QFs Sean Goddard. SFs Arne Huschenbeth. Final Yuta Takahashi. 15-1 overall, Champion.
2-1 in Draft, but only a single Modern win. No D2.
4-3 on D1, but a trememdous 6-1 on D2 took him into the T8. Lost the deciding game of the QFs to Marcio Carvalho.
One win in each format, out at 2-5.
Out at the earliest opportunity before winning a couple late.
Horrible 0-3 start, then six on the bounce, before Reid Duke eliminated him in R11. Still went 4-0-1 down the stretch in Modern.
Decent 2-1 in Draft 1, but 0-3 in Draft 2, and then lost the last three rounds to complete at 6-10.
Five wins in a row the highlight, but that was from a 1-3 hole.
Five straight wins to end D1 in good shape at 6-2, but a 2-5 reversal on D2.
Won four in a row, but still out before the return to Pioneer on D2.
A tale of two halves, going 2-1, 4-2, 7-2, and then enduring a miserable streak of seven straight losses.
Still made D2 from an 0-2 start, then a solid 5-3 on D2 without ever being in contention.
5-3 overnight, and a six round win streak kept him in contention to the very end, before Claire Rianhard won a R16 mirror match to eliminate him.
Draft pod win D1, 5-3 overnight, but no momentum in a 4-4 D2.
1-2 in Draft left him in trouble, and lost to Rei Hirayama in R7 to miss out on D2.
2-1 coming out of draft, but couldn't buy a win in Pioneer.
5-2 overnight, but already out of contention when he rattled off three wins to finish.
Highlight was trophy in D2, but a 3-6-1 Modern record was nowhere near sufficient.
Four straight D1 wins ensured D2, but soon out of the running.

A tremendous 6-1 looked like being squandered at 6-3, before another four straight wins. Beat Izzet Phoenix decks twice to reach the T8. Beat Alex Friedrichsen in the QFs before narrowly losing a remarkable SF to fellow Dane Simon Nielsen.
Never in the mix, and no D2.
5-2 and  6-3 before two losses ended his chances.
One win from each format, not close to D2.
Won three straight to reach 3-1, lost four straight to reach 3-5.
Had to win R8 to get there, but made the most of D2, going 6-2.
A slow 0-2 start rescued to 5-3 overnight, then into contention, winning his D2 Draft pod.Losses to Reid Duke and Daniel Goetschel meant he finished one round shy of T8.
Five wins to begin, a dominant Swiss performance meant T8 with two rounds to spare. Lost 3-1 in QFs to David Olsen.
From 2-2, a breathtaking 11 win streak to reach a second successive T8. Sadly, also a second successive QF loss, this time 3-1 to Dom Harvey with Amulet Titan.
5-2 overnight, but 0-3 in D2 Draft took him out of the running.
Three of his four losses were to Reid Duke, Marcio Carvalho, and Willy Edel. But four losses were also just enough to keep him out of the T8, despite winning his last five in a row.
Another huge win streak, this time nine rounds in a row. Another agonizing near miss, with Arne Huschenbeth the victor in their final round win-and-in.
Starting out 6-0 was the core of his run to T8, with four straight Modern wins on D2 sealing the deal. Once again there was a QF defeat, losing the deciding game to Simon Nielsen.

After three QF defeats, this time there was no mercy. From 2-2 he only lost once more. On Sunday, Ha Pham and Seth Manfield fell to him, before he swept aside Marcio Carvalho in the Final to become only the second two-time World Champion,
A useful 3-1 start, but two draws did him no favors, with his last of eight wins coming in R13.
Won his D1 Draft pod, fell away to 3-3, then ran up eight straight. That earned him two win-and-ins, but it was Jake Beardsley and Kai Budde who claimed the Sunday seats.
Just a single Draft win, before being eliminated at 1-4.
3-0 in Draft, 6-2 overnight, then 9-3. Luis Scott-Vargas and Brian Boss ended his chances, before he won his last two.
At 2-3-1 things looked bleak. He didn't lose again in the Swiss, winning nine on the bounce and reaching the T8. There, Yoshihiko Ikawa edged the deciding game to eliminate him in the QFs.
After a mediocre 4-3-1 on D1, he markedly improved with 6-1-1 on D2, the draws ultimately costing him a T8 berth.
A tough D1, eliminated in R6.
Trophy in Draft 1, so a disappointing 1-2 to open D2. 4-6 in Standard.
Solid 2-1 Draft, then 4-1 in Pioneer, before D2 1-2 in Draft used up his losses. Gavin Thompson-Exner functionally eliminated him in R12.
4-4 overnight, won his D2 Draft pod to reach 7-4, but fell away, only winning once back in Standard.
Costly Draw in R8, and a 1-2 Draft on D2 took him out of contention. Won all five Pioneer rounds to finish strong.
1-3, but managed to make D2. Won his last four this time to end 10-6, but was never in the running.
Deep 0-3 hole, but fought to reach D2. Never in the mix.
3-2, but lost his last two to miss out on D2.
Barely made D2, and 4-4 thereafter.
Four wins and a draw to start, but only mixed results from there. Jim Davis ended his run in R13.
Two stretches of three wins kept him in the mix until Modern on D2, but once there he only found a single win.
0-3 in Draft, and 3-1 in Standard couldn't save him.
4-1 was the high point, but kept winning enough to keep things interesting until the penultimate round, when Javier Dominguez ended his chances.
Had to win twice to reach D2, and might have wished he hadn't, going 2-6.
A swingy four wins  in a row, and three tough D2 defeats in a row. Ended up even at 8-8.
4-3 D1, improved to 5-2 D2, but not quite enough.
Survived an 0-3 Draft to reach D2, won seven of eight there, and still ended up one round away from T8.
5-3 D1, then 4-4 D2. Just never any real momentum.
3-0 Draft start, peaked at 5-0, but 3-4 on D2 kept him well away from T8.
Another perfect Draft start, but from 6-2 a reversal in Draft of 0-3 ended his hopes before D2 Pioneer.
Kept alternating wins and losses, until two losses in a row meant 3-5, and no D2.

Started 3-0 and never let up. 7-1 overnight, 2-1 in D2 Draft, and secured his T8 slot with a win over Marcio Carvalho in R15. Beat Chris Ferber in the QFs, before being swept by Benton Madsen in the Semis.
Dug a horrible 0-3 Draft hole, then won eight straight, including a perfect 3-0 D2 Draft, before the swingiest of tournaments ended with five straight losses.
Once again survived an opening 0-3 Draft, and again had a strong D2 at 6-2. But at 4-5, he was soon out of contention.
1-2 in Draft, and couldn't turn it round in Standard, meaning no D2.
Yet another 0-3 Draft, and this time it cost him a D2 place.

A nine win streak was the centerpiece of his run to T8, and this time Draft didn't get in the way, with an excellent 5-1 Limited record. Edged out Jason Ye in the QFs, but couldn't get past Yuta Takahashi in the Semis.
4-4 overnight became 7-4 after a Draft pod win on D2, but was soon out of contention once back in Modern.
Won his last two on D1 to advance, but couldn't get things going D2.
A solid 10-6, 5-3 both days, but not in the running after R12.
5-3 D1, but a trio of losses on D2 took him out of contention.
Heartbreaking. Literal constructed perfection of 10-0 neutered by 1-4-1 in Draft.
Alternated wins and losses until R7, when a fourth loss kept him out of D2.
Started out 0-3, so did well to make D2. Draft improved, going 2-1 on D2, but then no Standard wins.
Needed three straight to advance from 1-3, only managed one.
2-1 in Draft, but only one win in Standard.
0-3 Draft meant no D2.
3-0 Draft to start, ended D1 a brilliant 7-1. Couldn't convert, going 4-3-1 on D2 to miss out.
2-1 in Draft, but just a single Modern win. No D2.
Won D1 Draft pod, 6-2 overnight, again found D2 more challenging, going 3-5.
Only 4-4 overnight, 3-5 on D2.
Strong 6-2 D1, once again found D2 a struggle, going 3-5.
One win in each format, eliminated in R6.
Won three straight, but an unlikely Draft draw meant no D2.
Used up his losses by R10, won three in a row, before Marco Del Pivo ended his hopes in R14.
Deep trouble at 1-4, so credit for making D2. Also credit for 5-3 D2, but never in the mix.
4-4 D1, then a strong D2 highlighted by 4-1 in Modern.
After 2-1 in Draft, just one win in Standard, so no D2.
From R6-R12 he was unstoppable, turning 2-3 into 9-3. It took Nathan Steuer and Lotus Field Combo to end his chances in R15.
Four straight D1 defeats meant he needed two wins just to scrape into D2. Four Standard wins at the back end wasn't enough to contend.
Somehow forced a win-and-advance from an 0-4 start, but lost to Living End for an unlikely elimination.
From 4-1 to 4-3, but only lost once on D2 to reach the T8. After edging Greg Orange in the QFs, he swept both Anthony Lee and then Kazune Kosaka to claim the title.

Turned an 0-2 start well and truly around, finishing D1 at 6-2, then only losing once on D2 for the second tournament running. Went into the T8 unbeaten in Pioneer, but lost to the deck of the tournament (Rakdos Vampires) in the hands of Seth Manfield in the Quarterfinals.
Comfortably into D2, but a single point in Draft on D2 took him out of contention.
Tremendous 7-1 D1, but losses to Jason Ye and Javier Dominguez brought him back to the pack, and Sam Pardee eliminated him in R15 in the Bant Nadu mirror.
A perfect D1 to lead the field in defence of his title, but 0-3 in Draft D2 was damaging. Still played for T8 in the final round, but the legendary Kai Budde advanced.
Matching 4-4 records both days, never more than two wins on the bounce.

0-2 was a deep hole, but what a comeback. 5-3 overnight, a Draft pod win to start D2, then four of five in Modern took him into the T8. He defeated Javier Dominguez handily in the QFs, before losing to eventual Champion Jake Beardsley in the Semis.
1-2 in Draft, and eliminated by Takumi Matsuura in R6.
4-3-1 overnight, into contention with a D2 Draft pod win, before back to back losses against Yuta Takahashi and Shota Yasooka ended his interest.
2-1 in Draft, but only 1-4 in Standard. No D2.
Never two consecutive wins, lost his win-and-advance in R8.
Decent 2-1 in Draft, but lost his last three in Standard.
Disappointing, falling from promising 3-2 to elimation at 3-5.
A solid 2-1 into 6-2 on D1. Despite winning his last five on D2, he was already done, having gone 0-3 in Draft.
Only the minimum 4-4 D1, but a much better 6-2 D2. Never in contention, however.
2-1 in the opening Draft, but didn’t win a round in Modern, meaning no D2.
From a tenuous 4-3 to 7-4, before Sam Pardee eliminated him from contention in R12.
A decent 5-3 saw him out of contention at  6-5, before he swept his way through D2 in Pioneer, 5-0.
Won his Draft pod D1, ending at 6-2. 1-2 in Draft on D2 left him on the brink. Once again, a strong finish, winning his last four this time, wasn't enough.
An excellent 5-1 in Draft, but the damage was done in a 2-3 Modern record on D1. Yet another win streak (R10-14) in vain.
Always struggling, had a R7 match to try to advance, but missed out.
Only a single win from six rounds.
Had to win R8 to advance, then 2-6 on D2.
A strong 5-2-1 D1, but could only add a single win on D2 before dropping after R14.
Just a single Draft win to show from five rounds before dropping.
Tough road to reach D2, needing and getting wins ove Corey Burkhart R7 and Michael Belfatto R8. 3-5 on D2.
3-1 into 3-5 to miss D2.
Opened 0-4, and ran out of rounds, despite going 3-1 from there.
Decent 6-2 D1, but 3-5 D2.
4-2 turned into 4-5, and a five win streak on D2 was already too late.
Still in the mix heading back to Standard at 7-4, but 2-3 from there wasn't close.
Improved the minimum 4-4 into 8-4, before Brian Zilles ended his T8 interest in R13.
Average D1 at 4-3 improved to 5-2 D2, but ran out of rounds.

Made the most of playing the deck of the tournament. Six straight wins D1, six straight wins D2, into the T8 with two rounds to spare. And then ran into a horrible match against Mingyang Chen, losing the QFs in an 0-3 sweep.
5-3 overnight, before an 0-3 Draft D2 ended his interest.

5-3 D1 became 10-3. Beat Brian Boss and Jean-Emmanuel Depraz in the last two rounds to reach T8. Reversed an earlier loss to Jason Ye in the QFs, then won the decider against Eli Kassis in the Semis. Simon Nielsen beat him 3-1 in the Finals.
Not a D1 to remember, with a single Draft win the only highlight.
Perfect 6-0 in Draft, poor 3-7 in Modern.

Perfect 3-0 Draft to start, and in great shape at 7-1. 8-3 after Draft, he won three straight, getting him to the verge of T8. R15 saw him get there over Dan Kristoff, but he lost his QF to Benton Madsen.
Another strong D1 at 6-2, then 8-3, but two defeats took him out of contention.
Another 3-0 start, another 6-2, another Draft pod win, another push for T8. It took Alexander Hayne to finish him in R15.
5-1-1 D1, but three defeats early on D2 killed his chances.
A surprising 1-3, but still made D2 after four straight wins. Matched his 5-3 record from D1 on D2, but that wasn't enough.
Barely into D2 at 4-4, then 5-3 on D2.
2-1 in Draft, but didn’t win again until the final round of the day.
Turned an 0-2 start into 5-3 D1, but then only won once on D2.
6-3 early on D2, but then two more Draft losses took him out of contention.
Four straight D1 wins were the highlight, but 3-5 on D2 kept him firmly out of the mix.
1-2 became 5-2, but three straight D2 losses eliminated him.
2-1 in Draft, but no wins in Pioneer, so no D2.
Won his first round, but that was also his last win of the day.

Started 2-1 in Draft, then won seven in a row. Controversially Intentionally Drew with teammate Nathan Steuer in R11. Didn't cost him, reaching T8 with a round to spare. Lost deciding game of QFs to Claire Rianhard.
5-3 overnight, but a mixed D2 saw him out of contention early.
3-0 in Draft to start, but only one D1 Standard win. Soon out of contention on D2.
Only one win in each format, not enough for D2.
Only 4-3, before a seven win streak took him to the verge of T8. Lost his last two to just miss out.
4-4 became 7-4, before he fell out of contention early in Modern.
Just one win in five before packing them up.
Nice position at 6-2 after D1, but 4-4 D2.

Started winning his Draft pod, kept things going to 7-1, then got the Draft 6-0, leaving him in prime position for T8. Lost a couple of chances, but took the third, beating Simon Nielsen in R15 to reach the T8. Nielsen was waiting there, and soon had his revenge, sweeping Edelson out in the QFs.
Backed up his excellence from last time. Only just in contention at 5-4, won six of his last seven, with Lucas Duchow finally stopping him in R15.
Surprising 2-4 in Draft undermined him considerably, finishing 8-8.
3-1 in Standard came too late after a horror 0-3 Draft.
Won three straight, but that was it, leaving him one short.
Opened 2-0 in Draft, and had three chances to advance from 3-2, but couldn't take any of them.
Great start, opening 4-1, before losing five of the next six.
Plenty of back to back wins, but nothing dramatic, so out of the mix before the return to Standard.
2-1 in Draft, but out before the last round of the day.
4-4 on both days, even in both formats.
2-0 and 3-2, but lost his last two to miss D2.
Six straight wins D1, four straight D2, won his last two rounds to reach the T8. Lost narrowly to Reid Duke in QFs.

2-1, before setting off on yet another streak, this time encompassing nine wins and a draw. Still had to win his last round to reach T8, where he defeated Yiwen Chen, David Olsen, and finally Claire Rianhard en route to the title.
6-2 D1 before the wheels came off in a big way D2, with just a single match win.
Only a single match win.
Another streak took him from 2-2 to 6-2 overnight, but then the hard work was undone with an 0-3 Draft D2.
2-0, but that was all she wrote.
Two four round win streaks, before elimination by Claire Rianhard in R14. 5-1 in Draft the highlight.
Opened 2-1 in Draft, lost the last three in Modern to miss out.
Five wins in six midway through left him at 8-3, but only one D2 Pioneer win ended his chances.
The definitive 'game of two halves'. Overnight leader at 8-0, the top Draft table handed him three defeats on D2, and the losses kept on coming.
4-2 became 4-5 to leave him in the also-rans, but impressively swept D2 Modern with Golgari Yawgmoth.
His Constructed prowess continued from LOTR on D1 here, sweeping D1 Standard. He fell away after an 0-3 in Draft to open D2.
Needed a R8 win to secure his D2 berth, and then kept his hopes alive with a 3-0 in Draft. Toru Inoue ended his chances in R12.
An opening Draft 3-0 was squandered with just a single Standard win. Had an impressive 6-2 D2, but the damage was done.
Rightly proud of his record of always making D2, he needed three straight wins to maintain that, which he did. Won four in a row on D2 to end even at 8-8.
Perfect 3-0 start in draft, but 1-3 in Standard on D1, and only two further wins on D2.
1-2 Draft, 3-2 Pioneer, didn't reappear for D2.
A 3-0 Draft start turned into a horror show of six straight losses from R6-R11. Fought hard to 4-1 Pioneer D2, ending even at 8-8.
Turned 2-3 into 5-3, and, despite being out of contention early, won four of his last five.

A five win streak was the backbone of 6-2 on D1, and secured T8 thanks to four straight that included fellow T8ers Dom Harvey and Simon Nielsen. Eventual Champion Jake Beardsley brought his run to an end by 3-1 in the Quarterfinals.
Only one win in each format, nowhere near enough for D2.
Just alive heading into D2 Pioneer, he eliminated Paul Rietzl, Kenta Harane, and Theodore Jung, before Christoffer Larsen took care of business in R15.
Just like MKM, 7-4 heading into D2 Standard, again three more wins to 10-4 before a R15 elimination, this time to Sean Goddard.
Three times he had three straight wins, the last of which set up a win and in versus Daniel Goetschel in R16, with Goetschel taking the deciding game, and the T8 slot.
4-3 became 6-3, before Borja Yanez Carvajal beat him in both formats in the space of three rounds to end things.
Did well to reach D2 from 1-4, winning three straight, then went 2-6 D2.
D1 Draft trophy, then also perfect in Modern to pace the field at 8-0. Got to 9-0, but went 2-5 from there to miss out on T8.
Twice had four straight wins, but losses in R11-13 ended his chances.
4-1 - good. 4-5 - bad. Won his last three when well out of contention.
Won twice to reach D2, then 0-3 in Draft ended his chances.
Still alive at 7-4, but only won once back in Standard on D2.
3-1 became 4-4, out of contention early D2. Won his last three to finish even at 8-8.

From 2-1, was perfect 4-0 with Mono-Red. Another 2-1 in Draft kept him interested, and then two more constructed wins took him to T8. He swept Max Rappaport in the QFs, before narrowly losing to Marcio Carvalho in the Semis.
Perfect in Draft both days, but couldn't get above parity in Modern.
0-3 in Draft was too much to overcome.
Had to win R8 to reach D2, but was very solid once there, going 6-2 on the day, without ever being in contention.
Again in trouble at 2-3, but advanced to D2, and again had an excellent day, going 6-2.
Here we are again. 2-4 into 4-4, 6-2 D2.
Much better start at 5-0. Won his last three, but T8 was out of reach.
Excellent position at 8-2 before three straight losses eliminated him from the reckoning.
4-4 overnight. Won his D2 Draft, still alive at 8-4, before Nicole Tipple handed him the crucial fifth loss.
5-3 overnight, and another useful four round win streak kept him in it until R14, when Simon Nielsen ended things.
A frustrating D1, always up against it, and not quite advancing.

R1 was his only loss of D1 (with one draw), and astonishingly the same was true on D2, losing his opener to Logan Nettles, before six wins on the bounce took him to the T8. Lost 1-3 to Christoffer Larsen in the QFs.
5-1 in Draft, but not quite even in Standard, so no T8.
3-0 to start in Draft, but only 4-4 overnight, and a costly draw in R9 ended his chances.
5-2 D1, and live all the way to R13, where he lost to Shota Yasooka to end his chances.
Left rueing an 0-3 first Draft, because followed with seven straight. Later, won the last four rounds, but by then it was too late.
Rough start at 1-4, then won five straight, before five losses.
1-1 became 1-5.
Trophy in Draft 1, but 0-3 second time around.
Lost in R7 and R8 so no D2.
Outstanding 7-0 start, but it wasn't enough. Chris Ferber won their win-and-in in R16, leaving Inglis just outside the knockout rounds.
Strong 6-2 D1, and solid 5-3 D2. Still left him just shy of T8.
Battled back from 1-3 to make D2, but soon out of contention.
Out after just five rounds.
Just a single match win in a horrible D1.
4-0 start, but only 5-3 by the end of D1. Four losses early on D2 to end any chance.
Won back to back rounds four times, but never added a third.
Two starkly different formats. 1-5 in Draft, and a brilliant 9-1 in Standard. Rarely can pride and despair have balanced so perfectly.
5-2 overnight, then into contention with a 3-0 Draft sweep D2. Only won once back in Modern, however.
Opened 5-0, so 5-3 D1 was a disappointment. Still alive heading back to Pioneer, but Marco Del Pivo in R12 ended his T8 interest.
0-3 in Draft, but still scraped into D2, before another sub-par Draft eliminated him.
Arrived with no wins, left with no wins, at 0-5, eliminated at the earliest opportunity.
Saved his best performance of the season for the Big One. The minimum 4-3 overnight, he went 6-1 on D2, only losing to Kai Budde (no shame). Finished 10th, just outside the knockout rounds.
Out after R7, one win in each format.
Trophy in Draft 1, and solid 2-1 in Draft 2. 3-7 in Standard, however.
Work to do at 1-2, turned it into 8-2, but then fell away back in Modern.
From 1-2, went to 5-2 overnight, but eliminated R11.
Centerpiece was a rock solid six round streak. Brent Vos effectively knocked him out in R14.
Barely reached D2, improved 5-3 there, but never in the mix.
In the last chance saloon at 2-4, powered on to 7-4, before elimination from contention in R12.
Reached D2 with a final round win over Stefan Schutz, then only lost once on D2, winning his last six to reach the T8. Swept by Simon Nielsen in the QFs.
A middling D1, soon out of the running on D2, but had a decent four round streak in Pioneer.
Draft 3-0 to start, but two Draws weren't good. 4-4 D2 saw him finish mid-pack.
5-3 overnight became 8-3 with a Draft pod win. Seth Manfield eliminated him from T8 contention in R14.
From 2-1 in Draft, didn't win once in Standard, so no D2.
Four straight defeats mid-D2 ensured a losing record, including to Sam Pardee and Derrick Davis.

3-0 D1 Draft got the ball rolling before a first defeat to eventual Finalist Benton Madsen. 8-3 heading back to Pioneer, four straight wins, including a mirror against Gabriel Nassif, secured his T8 slot. Nathan Steuer and Derrick Davis fell, before he completed the assignment by sweeping aside Benton Madsen when it mattered most.

A slow 0-2 start still became a solid 5-3 D1, and he kept on winning, with six straight on D2, giving him two bites at the T8 apple. Daniel Goetschel and David Olsen had other ideas, and the defending PT champ fell one match short of T8.
A horror show on D1, with just one win in each format.

Perfect in Standard on D1, perfect in Draft on D2, a crushing performance that saw him into the T8 with three rounds to spare. Anthony Lee got in the way in the QFs, defeating him in the deciding game.
1-2 on D1 draft took time to repair, but after 3-0 in Draft D2 he was right in the mix. Losses to Luis Scott-Vargas and Brian Boss ended his hopes.
Strong 6-1-1 D1, but three straight Standard losses ended his contention.
A pair of 5-3s was fine, but never stringing together more than two wins left him well shy of the T8.
5-2 overnight, but couldn't get things going during a 3-4 D2.
Lone win came in Draft.
Terrific 6-1-1 on D1 melted into nothing with a 2-5-1 D2.
Even in Standard at 5-5, but 2-4 in Draft.
0-3 in Draft, 3-2 in Pioneer wasn't enough.
Seven of eight wins between R6 and R13 formed the bulk of Tobia's success, but Reid Duke eliminated him from contention in R14.
Got to 3-3, couldn't advance.
Already out at 4-5 before four straight wins pushed him to eventual parity.
Run of four, run of three, run of two, and a singleton made up ten wins. Just not quite enough to be in the T8 mix.
From 1-4, didn't lose again until R14.
Won last three of D1 to end 5-3, and kept alive as far as Pioneer on D2, where Logan Nettles ended his chances in R12.
4-1 and 6-2 were well  on track for T8. A 2-1 D2 Draft did no harm, but there were no Standard wins down the stretch.

Perfect 3-0 Draft to start, 7-1 overnight, and another positive Draft to start D2 2-1. Three straight wins down the stretch in Standard took him to the T8. There, he lost to Yuta Takahashi in the QFs.
It was a struggle to 3-3 before a four round burst lifted him into contention. Unfortunately it was followed by four straight defeats.
3-1 was good, and won three of the last four, but there were plenty of defeats in between, finishing 7-7.
Ended D1 with five straight wins, and ended D2 with three straight. 8-2 in Modern terrific, 2-4 in Draft the issue.
Won the opening round of Standard, but that was all.
Winning records in both formats, never lost two in a row, a really solid weekend.
So close. 3-0-1 in Standard, but an 0-3 Draft saw him fall short of D2.
Lost must-win R8, R7 draw proving costly.
Excellent 5-1 in Draf, but a deeply costly draw against Eli Kassis in R12 saw him fall agaonizingly short of Top 8.
After three straight losses, scraped into D2. Might have wished he hadn't, going 1-5 before packing it up.
6-2 D1 meant he was in contention heading back to Standard D2. 2-3 record there wasn't enough.
Matching 4-4 records, and an even split in both Draft (3-3) and Modern (5-5)

A career-best performance. First, only a single draw blemished an otherwise perfect D1. Despite two losses in three rounds to Reid Duke, he held his nerve, securing his T8 berth with a win over Eli Kassis. Got the one that really mattered against Reid Duke in the QFs, before eventual winner Jean-Emmanuel Depraz swept him in the Semis.
Could never quite get things going. 4-2 to 4-4, and out of contention at 6-5.
Middle of the pack throught, although 4-2 in Draft was solid.
4-4 again on D1 left him too much to do. Solid 5-3 D2.
Only one win in each format, not enough for D2.
4-1 became 4-5, and another four round win streak was too late to contend.
From 2-3, an excellent 8 of the next 9 left him live going into the penultimate round, before Toru Inoue ended his hopes.
From 1-3, won his last three on D1 to advance. Finished with an honorable 7-6-1 record.
Couldn't recover from an 0-3 Draft bomb, and two Pioneer draws didn't help his cause. No D2.
1-2 in draft, and eliminated from D2 by Jacob Nagro in R7.
0-3 in Ltd again, same result, no D2.
After a disastrous 0-3 Draft, won six of the next seven, before slipping away back in Modern.
Had to wait until R6 and R7 for wins.
Terrific start, opening 7-0. Came back to the field at 7-3, befoe securing T8 with a round to spare. Lost 3-1 to Arne Huschenbeth in the QFs.
Tremendous 7-1 D1, into disappointing 3-5 D2, with last win coming in R12.
3-2, but then lost three straight rounds to Esper Midrange opponents.
Didn't lose until R8, but an 0-3 Draft D2 left him against the wall. Won the first four back in Modern to play for T8 in R16, lost the deciding game to Matt Sperling.
Great start at 5-0. Won his D2 Draft pod, and his last three of D2, leaving him just short of T8.
3-0 Draft to start into 6-1-1 D1, but only a single Pioneer win D2.
5-3 D1, and five straight to finish D2, but by then was already out of the running.
Three draws on D1 cost him, but 8-5-3 was still solid.
A disastrous 0-5 to end the season.
Fought back from 1-3 to sneak into D2, where a 1-2 Draft ended his chances.
In prime position at 5-1, still in contention at 7-4, but then out early in Standard.
After a struggle D1 (4-4), a better 6-2 D2, although out of contention by the return to Modern.
2-1 in both Drafts kept him in contention to the penultimate round, where Alexey Paulot ended his run.

After a 4-1 start, a draw and loss looked like derailing things. He only lost once more, early on D2, before rattling off six wins to make T8. With the outstanding Rakdos Vampires, he was never in trouble in the elimination rounds, beating Jean-Emmanuel Depraz, Mingyang Chen, and finally Simon Nielsen, all by 3-1, to claim the title.
Turned 0-2 around in a hurry, ending D1 at 6-2. A 1-2 Draft on D2 didn't help, but it took Simon Nielsen in R14 to eliminate him from contention.
6-0 in Draft gave him the perfect springboard for another T8. But he was only 6-4 in constructed, and that became 6-5 when Eli Kassis handily won their QF.

From 1-1, won nine in a row, frankly astonishing at a World Championship, qualifying for T8 with three rounds to spare. In an absurdly talented T8, he fought past Kai Budde in the QFs before Javier Dominguez won their deciding game, thus claiming the Player of the Year title.
Kept going, and got a match win R6.
Lost the last two from 3-3 to miss D2.
Out of contention at the end of R9, but then won six of the last seven.
Got to 2-2, then 2-6.
Perfect 3-0 in Draft, kept winning multiple matches in a row, just finished one win short of T8.
Matching pair of 4-4s, couldn't get anything going.
From 0-2 to 3-3, but lost his last two, so no D2.
Awful. Five rounds, no wins, the end.
Promising 2-1 Draft, but lost both R7 and R8.
Ahead of the curve at 3-2, but couldn't get it done down the stretch.
Solid D1, but quickly out of contention on D2.
At 1-4, needed three straight wins. Only got two of them.
A swingy 8-8, with runs of five wins and three accounting for all eight, with plenty of famine in between.
On the brink at 2-4, won four straight before being out of contention before the return to Modern.
